newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill targets uninsured drivers.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill targets uninsured drivers.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said on Monday he signed legislation to require motorists in the state to show proof of auto insurance to renew their vehicle registration.
"This is an important step forward to get uninsured motorists off our roadways," Wilson, a Republican, said in a statement.
State lawmakers said the measure should reduce the number of uninsured drivers, blamed for a disproportionate share of accidents in the state.

The legislation requires motorists to show proof of insurance when stopped by police, otherwise their vehicle could be impounded or they could have their driver's license suspended and end up in county jail.

State officials estimated uninsured motorists in California cost insured motorists between $1 billion to $2.3 billion each year. Between 28 percent and 33 percent of motorists are uninsured in California, state insurance officials estimated.

"Californians already pay some of the highest insurance rates in the nation," Wilson said. "Uninsured motorists not only pose a threat to other drivers, but they also force the law abiding citizens of California to pay higher insurance premiums."
